method: 20 of 57 cited sentences (every third one) from 5 normal agent runs, each read against the source it cites. Checked by Claude (AI), not by a human expert.

checks.note: Ruxolitinib does block JAK1 (correct). But calls JAK1 'key' for Castleman; the source shows only a weak link (score 0.20).
Tofacitinib is a JAK inhibitor, as the source says.
The paper studied IL-6 antibodies' effect on mood; sirukumab was tested in arthritis, not in Castleman patients as the sentence implies.
Sirolimus acts on FKBP1A.
Everolimus acts on FKBP1A.
Imatinib acts on ABL1 and PDGFRB.
Nintedanib acts on PDGFRB.
Temsirolimus acts on FKBP1A.
Imatinib acts on ABL1.
Mechanism correct. 'Approved specifically for FOP' is true in reality but not in the cited source (came from memory).
Momelotinib acts on ACVR1, the protein behind FOP.
Mexiletine blocks SCN4A.
Lacosamide listed as acting on SCN4A.
Riluzole listed as acting on SCN4A.
Both papers name phenytoin as a treatment option for myotonia congenita.
BRAF is linked to Erdheim-Chester, but 'strongly' overstates the source's score (0.21).
Calls MEK1 'key'; the source shows a weak link (score 0.10).
'Key growth signals' is more than the weak link (0.10) in the source shows.
'Primary driver in many cases' is true in reality, but the source only gives a link score.
The phase 2 Erdheim-Chester trial is real; the 'phase 3' trial cited is a broad cancer trial, not specific to this disease.
